about.title: Sanger Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Sanger residents rely on a mix of local clinics and larger Fresno County medical centers, and most visits end with proper care. But when a provider misses a diagnosis, makes a surgical error, or mismanages medication, the harm can follow a patient for years. California law recognizes that not every bad outcome is malpractice — a claim generally requires showing the provider failed to meet the accepted standard of care and that failure caused real harm. Because these cases almost always need a qualified medical expert to explain what went wrong, and because California's MICRA rules set firm notice periods and deadlines, getting an early review matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect Sanger residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate hospital records, specialist notes, and pharmacy history to determine whether a case is worth pursuing, all without any upfront cost to the patient or family.

whyChoose.title: Why Sanger Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Deadlines Are Unforgiving
items.desc: California generally allows one year from when the harm was discovered, and no more than three years from the injury itself, to bring a claim — plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice to the provider. Missing these windows can end a case before it starts.

items.title: Expert Review Is Required
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert almost always has to confirm the standard of care was breached, an independent attorney familiar with this process can help gather the right records and specialists early.

items.title: Damages Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California's cap on non-economic damages rises each year under MICRA, and understanding how that cap applies to a specific case is something an independent attorney can walk a Sanger family through before deciding how to proceed.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Sanger?
items.answer: California generally gives one year from when you discover the injury, but never more than three years from when it happened. There's also a required 90-day notice to the provider before filing suit. Because these rules are strict, it helps to get a case reviewed sooner rather than later.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No — California law requires showing the provider's care fell below the accepted medical standard and that this failure caused the harm. A poor result alone, even a serious one, isn't enough on its own. This is why a qualified medical expert typically has to review the records.

items.question: Which Sanger medical providers does this cover?
items.answer: Claims can involve clinics, urgent care centers, and hospitals serving Sanger and the wider Fresno County area, whether the care happened locally or at a larger regional facility. An independent attorney can look at where and how the care was provided to determine the right next steps.

items.question: What does LawProactive charge for this service?
items.answer: Nothing — LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and attorneys in the network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. You can ask questions and get a case reviewed before deciding whether to move forward.
